notes: The tutorial uses the built-in LED on pin 13, so no external LED circuit is built.

The potentiometer straddles the breadboard centre gap in the image: two outer legs (GND and VCC, symmetric) are in columns 10 and 12 of the bank holding rows a-e (bank 't'), and the wiper (SIG) is in column 11 of the other bank ('b', row f). The yellow wire shares that strip at 11b.g.

Which outer leg goes to GND and which to 5V is taken from the image: the black wire is at column 10 and the red wire at column 12. The potentiometer is symmetric, so swapping them is electrically equivalent.
The black wire goes to the second GND pin on the power header (GND.2). The image labels the power header GND twice, and the black wire sits at the lower one.

The breadboard bank and row letters are mapped onto the catalogue naming, where rows a-e are bank 't' and rows f-j are bank 'b'. The image's row letters appear flipped, so this mapping is an assumption.
The USB cable is added as a power and programming connection. The image does not show it, and no ports are specified for it.

The MCP servers Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive need authorization. This session can't run OAuth, so they are unavailable until the user authorizes them in their claude.ai connector settings. This build did not use them.
